subject.title: Feature Request: One-click Anthropic authentication (OAuth flow)

question: Should OpenClaw expose Anthropic browser OAuth as a first-run onboarding/auth method, and what consent, scope, callback, token-storage, refresh, account-detection, and fallback contract is acceptable?
rationale: Source inspection can prove the current gap, but choosing to make Anthropic OAuth one-click crosses first-run UX, provider policy, and credential-security boundaries.

options.title: Add Provider-Owned OAuth After Approval
options.body: Expose an additive Anthropic OAuth auth method through the Anthropic plugin once the security, billing, docs, and fallback contract is approved.

options.title: Keep Explicit Auth Paths
options.body: Keep API-key, setup-token, and Claude CLI as the supported Anthropic setup paths and improve wording or docs instead of adding browser OAuth now.

options.title: Prototype Experimental OAuth
options.body: Allow a maintainer-owned experimental OAuth path that does not replace current Anthropic setup choices until live provider and security proof are strong.

recommendation.title: Add Provider-Owned OAuth After Approval
recommendation.body: Expose an additive Anthropic OAuth auth method through the Anthropic plugin once the security, billing, docs, and fallback contract is approved.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest feature-history signal on Anthropic setup-token and Claude CLI auth-choice behavior.
